question:
A 44-year-old woman attends a follow-up visit for management of menopausal hot flashes. Her medical
history includes hypertension, dyslipidemia, osteoporosis, and hypothyroidism due to Hashimoto's
disease. Three months ago, she was started on oral estradiol and micronized progesterone for hot
flashes, omeprazole for dyspepsia, and calcium for osteoporosis. She reports improvement in her hot
flashes and mood. On review of symptoms, she notes dry skin, occasional constipation, and mild
fatigue but denies dyspepsia, depressed mood, hair loss, or weight changes. She has not experienced
any falls or fractures. Her current medications include lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily,
alendronate 70 mg weekly, cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily, and levothyroxine 125 μg daily. Physical
examination is unremarkable. Laboratory results from 6 months ago and today are as follows: | | 6
months ago | Today | Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Thyroid-stimulating hormone (μU/mL) | 3.5 |
12.6 | 0.5–4.7 | | Total thyroxine (μg/dL) | 7.2 | 10.3 | 4.5–10.9 | | Sodium (mEq/liter) | 137 | 138 |
136–145 | | Potassium (mEq/liter) | 4.1 | 4.0 | 3.5–5.0 | | Chloride (mEq/liter) | 101 | 102 | 98–106 | |
Carbon dioxide (mEq/liter) | 22 | 23 | 21–30 | | Blood urea nitrogen (mg/dL) | 15 | 17 | 10–20 | |
Creatinine (mg/dL) | 1.0 | 0.9 | 0.6–1.1 | | Glucose (mg/dL) | 98 | 87 | 70–100 | What is the most likely
cause of the observed changes in this patient’s thyroid function tests? Answer Choices: (A) Initiation of
estradiol (B) Impact of changes in body weight (C) Interference from concurrent progesterone therapy
(D) Seasonal variation in thyroid function (E) Drug interaction with atorvastatin (F) Interaction between
alendronate and levothyroxine (G) Inadequate levothyroxine dose adjustment (H) Interference of
levothyroxine absorption by calcium supplementation (I) Progression of underlying Hashimoto's
thyroiditis (J) Drug interaction with omeprazole
 A. Interference from concurrent progesterone therapy
B. Interference of levothyroxine absorption by calcium supplementation

C. Interaction between alendronate and levothyroxine
D. Drug interaction with omeprazole
E. Initiation of estradiol
F. Impact of changes in body weight
G. Inadequate levothyroxine dose adjustment
H. Progression of underlying Hashimoto's thyroiditis
I. Drug interaction with atorvastatin
J. Seasonal variation in thyroid function
